Lower scores are better. Δ is the percent difference from SeasonalNaive when its score is positive. A negative difference is lower. W / T / L counts paired wins, ties and losses at each origin against SeasonalNaive. The counts give one vote per origin, while the aggregate score uses the selected metric’s weighting. Ranks use the unrounded scores.

Calibration and interval width

These diagnostics use the nine quantile forecasts on the selected cases. Coverage counts observations inside q10–q90, including both endpoints. With count data, ties at the endpoints can raise coverage above the nominal 80%, so read it alongside width. Scaled width divides q90 − q10 by the training activity scale. For discrete counts, compare whether the shares below and at or below q50 bracket 50%. The diagnostics use equal-series, equal-origin and equal-frequency averages.

Evaluation methods

The historical panel uses the frozen Impermanent sparsity labels. A case is one series at one origin. Daily origins have seven leads. Weekly and monthly origins have one lead.

Every model receives the observations available at its cutoff, with model-specific limits on usable context. Compatible models receive timestamp-derived calendar features. Locally fitted models use benchmark history available at each cutoff. SeasonalNaive is a fixed-rule reference.

Point metrics score each system’s submitted point forecast. The forecast-construction column shows when that point is the predictive median. Quantile metrics separately score the nine submitted quantiles. This retrospective comparison describes the models and forecast cases shown here.
